title: Explain a query plan without contacting a server
prompt: Write a standalone TypeScript ESM program that compiles a query into a deterministic execution plan using explainQuery from @honua/sdk-js/query-planner (planning is synchronous and side-effect free — no network). Use the descriptor { id: "parcels", protocol: "ogc-features", locator: { url: "https://example.test/ogc", collectionId: "parcels" }, capabilities: PROTOCOL_DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES["ogc-features"] } (capabilities from @honua/sdk-js/contract) and the query { where: "status = 'active'", outFields: ["parcel_id", "owner"], pagination: { limit: 100 } }. Inspect the first plan step: plan steps are a discriminated union on their engine property, and only steps with engine "remote" carry a compiled request (whose compiler property names the per-protocol compiler) — narrow the union before reading it. Print exactly one line to stdout: {"engine": <the first step's engine>, "compiler": <the first step's compiled request compiler id, or null when the step is not remote>, "hasFingerprint": <true when plan.fingerprint is a non-empty string>}.

context.notes: Golden workflow: explain-before-execute; the plan is a pure function of descriptor + query.
